bindings.label: Intermittent, dull, throbbing, localized tenderness in an alopecic patch on the right parietal-occipital scalp for 2-3 months

Patient is a woman in her early twenties with a lifelong history of alopecia; the affected right parietal-occipital scalp alopecic patch has been stable in size and appearance since birth, and three other round alopecia patches present since birth remain asymptomatic
Clinical scalp examination revealed an atrophic white patch of alopecia, with ill-defined bogginess surrounding the lesion and extending to the central and posterior occipital scalp
Dermoscopy shows translucent epidermis, branched vessels, and marginal hair bulbs
Head CT shows no osseous, vascular, neural, or soft-tissue defects
Aplasia cutis congenita of the scalp
